sections.overview: Nomura jellyfish is a large scyphozoan in the family Rhizostomatidae.
sections.identification: It can reach about 2 metres in bell diameter and 200 kilograms in wet mass, although such maxima are exceptional.
sections.habitat: Its range includes the Bohai, Yellow, East China and Japan seas; currents can carry medusae from spawning areas toward Japan and Korea.
sections.diet: Korean fisheries information reports that it consumes zooplankton and fish eggs, but the relative importance of these foods is not quantified there.
sections.behavior: At one Japan Sea study site, most observed medusae stayed above roughly 40 metres during daytime; this result is local, not a universal depth limit.
sections.reproduction: Benthic polyps release young medusae seasonally, with April–June release reported in the Yellow and East China seas.
sections.ecology: Its mass appearances are irregular, and drifting blooms can obstruct fishing gear and damage fisheries across East Asia.
sections.conservation: The Korean national marine species list does not mark it as a marine protected species; this says nothing about its status in other countries.
